name: AMD Instinct MI325X / MI350X: Passive OAM cooling makes direct-to-chip liquid cooling mandatory at 1000 W TBP
region: Global; via OEM partners (Supermicro, Dell, HPE and others per the existing amd-instinct-oem-systems record)
notes: THE AMD HALF OF THE LIQUID-COOLING STORY, AND IT IS CLEANER AND HARDER THAN THE NVIDIA ONE. AMD's own product pages for both parts state, under Board Specifications, 'Cooling: Passive OAM', and under Requirements, 'Typical Board Power (TBP) 1000W (TBP)' for MI350X and 'Typical Board Power (TBP) 1000W Peak' for MI325X, with 'External Power Connectors 54V UBB' for both. PASSIVE OAM IS THE DECISIVE SPECIFIER AND IT IS NOT SUBTLE: a passive OAM module has no integrated heat sink and no fan of its own, so it physically cannot reject 1000 W unaided. It requires a cold plate bonded to it in the host chassis, which requires a liquid loop in the server, which requires a CDU or facility liquid in the rack. So the same hard procurement fact that applies to GB200 NVL72 applies here, and it applies at 1000 W per module - i.e. an 8-module MI350X platform is an ~8 kW GPU load that is nonetheless a LIQUID-COOLED system, not an air-cooled one. This is the trap in the MI300-series line: the parts are usually discussed by memory capacity and FLOPs, and the cooling requirement is the fact most likely to be missed, because '1 TB of HBM3E' says nothing about needing a wet loop. COMPARISON WORTH KNOWING, RECORDED AS A CONTESTED PAIR RATHER THAN RECONCILED: AMD's own MI325X collateral footnotes 'the NVidia Blackwell HGX B100 (192GB) 700W GPU accelerator' and 'HGX B200 (192GB)' - i.e. AMD quotes 700 W for B200 in its comparison footnotes, while NVIDIA's Blackwell datasheet publishes Max TDP 'Configurable up to 1,000 W' for HGX B200 and up to 1,200 W for GB200 NVL72/NVL4. The split is knowable: AMD is quoting a nominal sustained figure and NVIDIA is publishing a configurable ceiling. Anyone doing a cross-vendor power budget should ask which they are holding, because a 700 W assumption against a 1,000-1,200 W reality is a 40-70% sizing error. GENERATION NOTE: MI325X and MI350X share the identical 1000 W TBP and Passive OAM envelope, so they fall in the same procurement bucket - a host validated for one is thermally valid for the other, and there is no cooling-requirement change across the CDNA3 to CDNA4 transition. Note also '54V UBB' is the same 50-51V-class rack busbar distribution NVIDIA's GB200 power shelves convert down to, so a facility designed for one vendor's rack-scale system has infrastructure that is partly relevant to the other - though the manifold and cold-plate mechanics are not interchangeable.
